correctness.rationale: All edge gradients are exactly the bounded zero-sum arrays; quotient duality gives the median absolute-deviation norm. A strictly positive irreducible tridiagonal evolution proves radial heat-kernel ordering. Radial counting fixes the median at distance k=floor((n+2)/4) and yields a feasible, simultaneous sharp gradient. The unique length-k walk gives heat mass t^k/k!+O(t^(k+1)), and all outer masses are O(t^(k+1)); hence the exact 4k+2-n defect. Strict positivity and semigroup submultiplicativity give strict decrease. All steps hold for every integer n>=5 and every real t>=0. Checks: 60 direct LP instances, 15 exact symbolic coefficients, and 288 strict radial comparisons. These finite tests are corroborating, not the proof.
